extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (also useful to patent practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Form-paragraph guidance and substantive legal standards for drafting and issuing rejections, restriction requirements, and double-patenting/112 issues in U.S. design patent prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103(a) rejection — design disclosed but not claimed in another application with common inventor/assignee (¶15.19.03.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use when the claim is provisionally rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as obvious over a copending application with a common inventor/assignee that has an earlier effective U.S. filing date and would constitute prior art under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) if published or patented; this rejection is based on a presumption of future publication or patenting of the conflicting application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although not identically disclosed, if differences would render the claimed subject matter obvious to a designer of ordinary skill, the invention is unpatentable. Overcoming options: show derivation under 37 CFR 1.132 (design in reference derived from this application's designer), show date of invention prior to reference under 37 CFR 1.131(a), or for applications filed on/after Nov 29, 1999 show common ownership/obligation of assignment (see MPEP §§706.02(l)(1),(2)). Use pre‑AIPA/pre‑AIA date rules per MPEP; for apps claiming priority to pre‑Mar‑16‑2013 filings, precede with form paragraph 15.10.15. Examiner notes: insert serial numbers/inventor/assignee and provide an obviousness explanation (bracketed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103(a) rejection — design claimed in earlier‑filed design application with common inventor/assignee (¶15.19.04.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use when the claimed design is obvious over the design claimed in an earlier‑filed copending design application that has a common inventor/assignee; because of the earlier effective filing date and different inventive entity it would be prior art under pre‑AIA 102(e) if patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a provisional obviousness‑type double patenting rejection as well. Provide serial numbers and inventor/assignee in brackets and an explanation of obviousness/differences (follow with form paragraphs 15.70.fti and 15.67 or 15.68). Must be preceded by form paragraph 15.19.02.fti and, for certain priority situations, 15.10.15.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2)/103 rejection — design disclosed, no common inventors/assignees (¶15.19.05.aia)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject under 35 U.S.C. 103 as obvious over a reference which, because it names another inventor and has an earlier effective filing date, is prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overcoming the rejection may be done by: (1) showing under 37 CFR 1.130(a) that the copending application's subject matter was obtained from the inventor (so not prior art under 102(b)(2)(A)); (2) perfecting a 35 U.S.C. 119 priority claim by filing certified priority documents that satisfy 35 U.S.C. 112(a); (3) perfecting a 35 U.S.C. 120 benefit claim via an application data sheet per 37 CFR 1.76 and establishing the prior application satisfies 112(a); or (4) showing a prior public disclosure under 37 CFR 1.130(b) (102(b)(2)(B)). Insert document numbers and provide full obviousness explanation in brackets. For priority to pre‑Mar‑16‑2013 filings, precede with form paragraphs 15.10.aia and 15.10.15.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103(a) rejection — design disclosed but not claimed (¶15.19.05.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as obvious over a reference that discloses the design (e.g., in drawings) but does not claim it; the reference constitutes prior art under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) based on earlier effective U.S. filing date/different inventive entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designs in drawings (including broken lines or subcombinations) can render a later design obvious. Overcoming options: derivation under 37 CFR 1.132, date of invention under 1.131(a), or showing common ownership/assignment for apps filed on/after Nov 29, 1999 (MPEP §§706.02(l)(1),(2)). Use pre‑AIPA 102(e) date rules with AIPA exceptions; insert reference numbers and an explanation of obviousness and differences (follow with form paragraphs 15.70.fti and 15.67 or 15.68). For priority issues, precede with 15.10.15 when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103(a) rejection — design claimed in design patent with earlier effective filing date and common assignee (¶15.19.06.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as obvious over the claim in an earlier design patent with an earlier effective filing date; based on different inventive entity it constitutes prior art under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be overcome by submitting an oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131(c) stating current common ownership and that the inventor named is the prior inventor under 35 U.S.C. 104 (as in effect Mar 15, 2013). A terminal disclaimer under 37 CFR 1.321(c) is also required. An obviousness‑type double patenting rejection must be included. Provide patent numbers and an explicit obviousness explanation (follow with form paragraphs 15.70.fti and 15.67 or 15.68). For certain priority situations precede with 15.10.15.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggestion to overcome 35 U.S.C. 112(a)/(b) rejections in design applications — convert indefinites to broken lines (¶15.20.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may overcome 35 U.S.C. 112(a)/(b) rejections (indefiniteness/nonenabling) by disclaiming indefinite/nonenabling areas of the design by converting them to broken lines and amending the specification to state the broken‑line portions form no part of the claimed design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a different form paragraph for international design applications (form paragraph 29.27). Insert the article title in bracket. This form paragraph must be preceded by 15.19.02.fti where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) and (b) — claim not enabled/indefinite (¶15.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject when the claimed invention is not described in full, clear, concise, and exact terms to enable a person skilled in the art to make and use it (35 U.S.C. 112(a)) and/or fails to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter (35 U.S.C. 112(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State that the claim is indefinite/nonenabling and provide full explanation of basis for rejection in the bracketed text. For apps with filing dates on/after Mar 16, 2013 that claim priority to pre‑Mar‑16‑2013 filings, precede with 15.10.15.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combined 35 U.S.C. 112(a)/(b) and pre‑AIA 103 rejection when earlier design patent exists with no common assignee (¶15.19.07.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use when the claim is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(a)/(b) as not enabled or indefinite and also rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) over a design patent having an earlier effective filing date and no common assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a complete explanation of the basis for the 112 rejection in the bracketed area. Do not use this paragraph when separate rejections under 112(a) or (b) are appropriate. Insert patent number and explain differences for obviousness (follow with form paragraphs 15.70.fti and 15.67 or 15.68). Precede with 15.10.15 where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 112(b) second paragraph — additional information requested when title ambiguous (¶15.21.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use when the claim is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) second paragraph because the title of the article in which the design is embodied is too ambiguous to permit proper examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request applicant to provide sufficient explanation of the nature and intended use of the article, and any helpful additional information (analogous fields of search, pertinent prior art, advertising brochures, filing of copending utility applications and utility application number if any). Warn that clarifying the title by specifying the article may introduce new matter (35 U.S.C. 132; 37 CFR 1.121).

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 171 double patenting rejection (design-design) — statutory double patenting (¶15.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject under 35 U.S.C. 171 when a claim is claiming the same design as that claimed in an earlier United States Design Patent (statutory double patenting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advise that information addressing the rejection should be submitted as a separate paper and not inserted into the specification (37 CFR 1.56). Form paragraph 15.23.02 (summary for 'same invention' type double patenting rejections) should follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 112(b) second paragraph — scope cannot be determined (¶15.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use this form paragraph when the scope of the claimed design cannot be determined and the claim is indefinite under 35 U.S.C. 112(b)/pre‑AIA 112 second paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a full explanation of the basis for the rejection in the bracketed text. This is used where the examiner cannot determine the scope from the claim/drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Or the like' / 'or similar article' indefinite claim rejection (¶15.22.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) second paragraph when the use of phrases like '--or the like--' or '--or similar article--' following the title creates indefiniteness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancellation of the phrase in the claim and each occurrence throughout the papers (except the oath/declaration) will overcome the rejection (see Ex parte Pappas). Do not use this where the phrase is directed to the environment of the article embodying the design. Insert the exact phrase in the bracket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title fails to specify a known article of manufacture — 35 U.S.C. 112(b) rejection (¶15.22.03)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject when the claim title fails to identify an article of manufacture and the drawing disclosure does not inherently identify the article in which the design is embodied, rendering the claim indefinite under 35 U.S.C. 112(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite Ex parte Strijland. Request clarification from applicant; warn about introduction of new matter if title is changed in the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 171 provisional double patenting rejection (design-design) (¶15.23.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisionally reject under 35 U.S.C. 171 when the claim is claiming the same design as that claimed in a copending application (conflicting claims not yet patented).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark as provisional because the conflicting claims have not been patented. Form paragraph 15.23.02 should follow all 'same invention' type double patenting rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary for 'same invention' type double patenting rejections — terminal disclaimer not available (¶15.23.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory that a terminal disclaimer may not be used to overcome a 'same invention' type double patenting rejection (where priority of invention bars issuance of more than one patent for the same invention).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite case law (In re Thorington) and MPEP § 804.02. This form paragraph should follow all 'same invention' type double patenting rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonstatutory double patenting rejection (single reference) — patentably not distinct (¶15.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject for nonstatutory double patenting where the conflicting claims are not identical but are not patentably distinct from each other because the differences are minor and do not distinguish the overall appearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify prior patent number and explain why differences are minor and not distinguishing. This paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 15.24.06 and followed by 15.67. Insert differences in bracketed text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional nonstatutory double patenting rejection (single reference) (¶15.24.03 / ¶15.24.06)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisionally reject on nonstatutory double patenting grounds over a copending application/patent where the conflicting claims are not patentably distinct; provisional because the conflicting claims have not been patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify conflicting application number and specify the minor differences. Precede with 15.24.06 and follow with 15.67.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional nonstatutory double patenting rejection (multiple references) (¶15.24.04)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisionally reject on nonstatutory double patenting of a copending application in view of one or more secondary references; assert that it would have been obvious to a designer to modify the copending claim as demonstrated by secondary references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the copending claim is modified and identify secondary references that teach the modifications. Explain the judicial policy basis for the doctrine and note that a timely filed terminal disclaimer under 37 CFR 1.321(c) may overcome an actual or provisional nonstatutory rejection if common ownership is shown (37 CFR 1.131(c)). Provide information about eTerminal Disclaimers (USPTO forms and web‑based eTD). Precede with 15.24.06 and follow with 15.68.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identical claim with common assignee — priority issues and abandonment risk (¶15.24.05.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the claim is directed to the same invention as a commonly assigned copending application, resolve priority under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(f)/(g); terminal disclaimer has no effect because the basis for refusal is priority (not extension of monopoly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignee must state which entity is the prior inventor; failure to comply may result in abandonment. This paragraph should precede all nonstatutory double patenting rejections as a heading (except 'same invention' type).

rubrics_metrics.name: Double patenting rejection (design‑utility) — design claim overlaps utility claim (¶15.24.07 / ¶15.24.08)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject under the judicial doctrine of double patenting when a design claim is directed to the same invention as a claim of a utility patent (or copending utility application) — may be provisional if the conflicting claims are not yet patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite In re Thorington. Form paragraph 15.23.02 should follow all 'same invention' type double patenting rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonstatutory double patenting rejection (multiple references) — grouping of patentably distinct embodiments (¶15.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple embodiments are disclosed, identify patentably distinct groups of designs; if embodiments are patentably distinct they must be restricted to separate prosecution and cannot be included in one design application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how embodiments divide into groups and why differences are not minor or are patentably distinct. Provide bracketed identification of conflicting patent number, secondary references, modifications, and which secondary references teach modifications. Precede with 15.24.06 and follow with 15.68.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of prior application(s) in nonprovisional applications — claiming benefit requirements (¶15.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: To claim the benefit of a prior‑filed application, a continuation or divisional must include a specific reference to the prior application in compliance with 37 CFR 1.78; placement depends on filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed before Sep 16, 2012 include the specific reference in the first sentence(s) of the specification following the title or in an application data sheet; if filed on/after Sep 16, 2012 include the specific reference in an application data sheet. For benefit claims under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c), the reference must include the relationship (continuation, divisional, continuation‑in‑part).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction requirement under 35 U.S.C. 121 — patentably distinct embodiments (¶15.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction to one patentably distinct group of designs is required when multiple embodiments disclosed in a design application are patentably distinct and do not constitute a single inventive concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reply must include election of a single group for prosecution on the merits (37 CFR 1.143); replies that do not include an election will be held nonresponsive. If applicant traverses the requirement, present evidence now showing the groups are obvious variations. If groups are later determined not patentably distinct, arguments asserting patentability based on differences between groups will not be considered. Action on the merits is deferred pending compliance (Ex parte Heckman). Provide brackets for embodiments and explanations of differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction under 35 U.S.C. 121 — obvious variations within a group and when restriction not required (¶15.27.01–.03)
rubrics_metrics.description: Embody guidance for determining when multiple disclosed embodiments are patentably indistinct and may remain in the same application (change in appearance), versus when they form patentably distinct groups requiring restriction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If embodiments within a group have overall appearances that are basically the same and differences are minor or shown obvious in view of analogous prior art, they are considered obvious variations and retained in the same application; any rejection of one embodiment applies equally to others and arguments based on differences will not be considered once groups are determined to comprise a single inventive concept. Examiner notes indicate where to insert embodiments, groups, and explanations of differences.
